title: Ash-Shahid, the Witness
tomorrow: Amira told her dad it went 'great!' was that true?

cards: A lobby with gray chairs and a ticking wall clock, finalists pretending to read their notes. Amira came straight from her chem test, and her hands are cold.
Across the room, Kayla is patting every pocket: her ID is gone, and they won't let her in without it. Amira spots it under a chair and hands it over. Nobody from the panel sees.
Then Amira's name is called, she walks in, and she blanks on the second question. So who saw the part that mattered?

teach.b: The Qur'an has a Name for that: Ash-Shahid, the Witness. In Surah An-Nisa: "And Allah is sufficient as Witness." A witness isn't a judge, and isn't a camera.
A witness is someone present, who can later say: I was there, and this is what happened. The panel saw a blank on question two.
Ash-Shahid saw the ID under the chair, the chem test that morning, the weeks of versions, the nerves in the lobby. The fullest account of the day belongs to the Witness, not the panel.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, gave this its sharpest form. In the hadith of Jibril, in Sahih Muslim, he's asked what ihsan is, doing things beautifully.

teach.h: IF YOU DON'T SEE HIM, HE SEES YOU.
teach.b: His answer: that you worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, He sees you. Notice the order. First, act as if you see.
And if that's too much today, rest in being seen. That's what acting as witnessed means. Not performing for an audience.
An audience sees a performance; a Witness sees a life. Just doing the thing well, because Someone is present for all of it. Here's the detail to tell a friend tonight.
The declaration of faith in Islam is called the shahada, the bearing of witness.
Muslims say it with their own mouths, in each prayer's sitting. The Witness, and a people who witness back.

how: Muslims bear witness in the shahada, said on entering Islam and repeated in the tashahhud of each prayer; ihsan, worshiping as though you see Allah, is taught from the hadith of Jibril.

o: the one who punishes what's done in secret
the one who writes each deed down in ink
the Witness, present to all that happens

games.q: seen and witnessed — tap the pairs.

s: in the hadith of Jibril, ihsan is to worship as though you see Him
and if you don't see Him, He sees you (Sahih Muslim).
Ash-Shahid mainly means God judging what you did in secret
a witness is present and can tell what happened: "Allah is sufficient as Witness" (4:79).
only what the panel sees really counts
the lesson's point: the Witness sees the whole morning, the ID under the chair included.

games.q: your coworker leaves early and asks you to log their hours as a full shift. the manager never checks. what fits today's Name?
o: log the real hours. Someone is present even when the manager isn't.
log the full shift; it's harmless if nobody ever checks.
log it this once, and warn them it's the last time.
games.why: ihsan, from the hadith of Jibril: act as though you see Him, and if not, He sees you. the Witness is present when the manager isn't.

practice: Close your eyes and sit as if someone kind is in the room with you, watching without judging. Let your shoulders settle the way they do around a person who already knows you. Nothing to prove, nothing to perform.
If your mind runs to what went wrong today, let it, and let that be seen too. Stay there, simply seen, until the bell.

wordCard.voice: Ash-Shahid. The Witness, present to all of it, the whole morning and not just question two. Name fifty.

orig.note: Arabic: the Witness. the shahada, the declaration of faith, is a bearing of witness.

carryVoice: The line: witnessed, because the panel saw one answer and the Witness saw the whole morning. Fifty names now.

sources.q: And Allah is sufficient as Witness.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 8 (the hadith of Jibril: ihsan is to worship Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you)
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3507 (the list of the Names, including ash-Shahid)
